simplicity.feedback: Excellent simplicity with clear single goals and consistent structure. Very manageable for Grade 1.
strengths: Each lesson has ONE clear, achievable goal
Consistent 3 decision points format maintained
Substitute-friendly with clear instructions
Age-appropriate timing and expectations
Simple vocabulary introduction (3 words max per lesson)
improvements: Some lessons could use more specific material alternatives
Could simplify a few technical reading concepts further

progression.feedback: Strong logical progression from text identification to comprehension strategies. Good scaffolding throughout.
strengths: Clear progression: identification → prediction → comprehension → analysis
Vocabulary builds systematically (texte → image → prédire → comprendre)
Good mix of receptive and expressive activities
14 core lessons systematically cover reading expectations
Extensions provide meaningful enrichment
improvements: Could reinforce some key vocabulary more frequently
Some lessons feel slightly disconnected from previous ones

authenticity.feedback: Very authentic approach that respects Grade 1 developmental needs and classroom realities.
strengths: Realistic expectations for beginning French learners
Flexible approaches for different learning styles
Good troubleshooting for common classroom scenarios
Meaningful real-world connections throughout
Respects silent period for language learners
Practical activities teachers can actually implement
improvements: Could include more specific differentiation strategies
Some activities might need more visual support details

strengths: Excellent scaffolding from pictures to words to comprehension
Age-appropriate introduction to reading strategies
Strong emphasis on prediction and questioning
Good balance of fiction and non-fiction exploration
Celebrates diverse text types and cultural backgrounds
Practical activities that build real reading skills
Appropriate use of detective/exploration themes for engagement
concerns: Some comprehension concepts might be advanced for early Grade 1
Portfolio creation in Lesson 14 might be complex for some students
recommendations: Add more specific visual support descriptions
Include simple assessment strategies for reading growth
Provide more concrete examples of text types for teachers
Add more movement-based activities for kinesthetic learners

usabilityRating.substituteTeacher: Very Good - clear enough for implementation with brief prep
usabilityRating.newTeacher: Good - would benefit from additional reading strategy resources

ageAppropriateness: Very Good for Grade 1 French Immersion - respects developmental stage
